# s225 — Make the suite refuse to run against the enclosing real project

A test fixture whose own project is missing must stop with a clear error, not fall through to the real project that encloses it, because the suite can then edit the tracking state it is checking.

**Findings:** s224 landing 2026-10-05: a full-suite run from the main checkout root failed 560 tests and wrote into the real .slicer/ · **Size:** M · **Tree:** tests

**2026-10-05** — Reproduced in disposable nested fixtures: an enclosing Git MERGE_HEAD makes child init exit 2 before creating .slicer/config.json. After clearing the enclosing merge marker, child add previously exited 0 and changed the enclosing fixture index. This matches the recorded merge-in-progress symptom; no production discovery changes are needed. The exact concurrent sequence from 2026-10-05 was not replayed.

**2026-10-05** — Ready for review: fixture discovery guard and five regressions implemented. Full suite passed: 1205 tests, one optional skip; copied real tracking-state check, slicer check and git diff --check passed. Changes remain uncommitted in feature/s225-fixture-guard. Corrected the earlier done status at the owner’s request; review and landing remain pending.

**Not in this slice:** changing production discovery in `src/slicer/store.py`, changing `init`, removing the in-checkout `TMPDIR` advice, hiding enclosing projects suite-wide (S54 kept `isolated_discovery` scoped on purpose), or repairing already-polluted tracking state.

## Why

On 2026-10-05, `TMPDIR="$PWD/.venv/test-tmp" python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests` run from the main checkout root, with an s224 merge in progress and another agent running the suite from `.worktrees/s182`, ended `FAILED (failures=560, errors=268)` in about 60s; a normal run takes 150 to 220s. A second run with a private `TMPDIR` failed the same way (564 failures, 268 errors). The first error seen was `FileNotFoundError` for `<fixture>/.slicer/index.json`.

The tests also changed the real project: notes added to S01, a `ghost` pass set on it, S05 removed, `done/S99.json` moved, and `log.jsonl` appended. That state was restored from the staged merge. The same commit passes in a throwaway clone (`test_Add_NewlineInShortTitle`), in the s224 worktree, and in a detached scratch worktree (1200 tests OK). So the code is sound, and some state of the main checkout made fixtures lack their own `.slicer`. That cause is not identified. `TempRepo.run` passes `--root` for the fixture, but nothing checks that the project the command resolves to is the fixture. S54 added `support.isolated_discovery` as an opt-in only.

## Files

- `tests/support.py` (`TempRepo.run`)
- a new test module for the guard, for example `tests/test_support_isolation.py`
- `AGENTS.md` (how to run the suite) only if the cause stays unexplained

## Failing tests

1. `test_TempRepoRun_ProjectResolvesOutsideFixture_RefusesBeforeRunning`: a fixture directory inside a directory that has its own `.slicer/config.json`, with no `.slicer` of its own. `TempRepo.run("add", "x")` raises a test error naming the fixture and the project it would have used. The enclosing project's index and log are byte-identical afterwards.
2. `test_TempRepoRun_InitInEmptyFixture_StillWorks`: `run("init")` in a fresh fixture is allowed, and later commands resolve to the fixture.
3. `test_TempRepoRun_IsolatedDiscovery_StillAllowsOutsideProjectFixtures`: tests that use `support.isolated_discovery` keep working unchanged.
4. The full suite passes unchanged apart from tests that deliberately discover a parent project. Each of those opts out by name in the test, and the slice lists them.

## Implement

First, try to identify why a fixture lacked its own `.slicer` in the 2026-10-05 runs. Work only in a throwaway clone or a scratch worktree, never in the real checkout's `.slicer/`. Record what is found, or that it was not reproduced, in a note on the item.

Then add the guard in `TempRepo.run`, before `main()` runs: unless the command is `init` or the test opts out, resolve the project the way `store.discover` would from the fixture root, and raise if it is not the fixture root. Name both paths in the message. Keep the opt-out explicit and per test. Do not change `store.discover` or the CLI.

If the cause is still unknown after the guard lands, add one line to `AGENTS.md` saying to run the suite from a worktree or clone, with the date and symptom.

## Check

Run the suite from a worktree or a throwaway clone, not the main checkout root: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests`, plus `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m slicer check --json` and `git diff --check`. Then run guard tests 1 and 2 against a fixture inside a directory holding a copy of a real `.slicer/`, and confirm that copy is unchanged.

Explicit guard opt-outs are per call in `test_About_NoProject_PrintsTextWithoutDiscovery` (`tests/test_cli.py`) and `test_SetupGit_NeedsNoProject_NeverLoadsOrLocks` (`tests/test_merge.py`), because those tests mock discovery itself. The new `test_TempRepoRun_ExplicitParentDiscovery_OptsOutForOneCall` (`tests/test_support_isolation.py`) deliberately discovers a disposable parent and proves the next call is guarded again. Other no-project tests use scoped `support.isolated_discovery` rather than opting out.
